newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Ruehe warns cuts could hurt Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Ruehe warns cuts could hurt Eurofighter.

text.p: Defence Minister Volker Ruehe warned on Friday that further cuts in the defence budget could undermine Germany's commitment to the Eurofighter.

Ruehe said Finance Minister Theo Waigel must keep the promises he made last year to boost the defence budget, partly to finance the Eurofighter, a jet fighter being developed together with Britain, Spain and Italy.
The government must review the matter by July 2, when the budget for 1998 is to be prepared, he said.
"We need (Eurofighters) starting in 2002. The matter was negotiated with the industry based on ... financial promises made last November," Ruehe said. "These must now be kept."
Ruehe said even the austerity measures the government was undertaking to meet the requirements for European monetary union would not affect the defence budget.
"There is no place else to cut. On the contrary, we have a promise of a small increase in the next few years," he said.
Tight finances had crimped military investment, but would not lead to a restructuring of the German army, he said.
"I am sure there would be no (parliamentary) majority for the destruction of the German army as we know and value it."
Ruehe said he would stand by his decision that no German soldiers should be sent to Albania.
The Eurofighter's German partner, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, has said 18,000 jobs depend on building the combat jet.
The other partners in the project are British Aerospace, Alenia Spa of Italy and Spain's state-owned CASA.

Ruehe had negotiated a price tag of 23 billion marks for the batch of Eurofighters Bonn wants to buy, pricing each aircraft at 125.4 million marks. Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) say the money could be better spent elsewhere.
